name: legal-research-and-analysis
title: Legal Research and Issue Analysis
description: Analyze a legal question against governing documents, authorities, facts, and requested conclusions.
procedure:
1. Identify the precise issue and controlling time, jurisdiction, and document set.
2. Extract the governing rule or clause and the facts that trigger it.
3. Apply each element to the supplied facts, preserving material uncertainty.
4. State the conclusion and the evidence supporting it without inventing authority.
notes: Distinguish the source's rule from your application and conclusion.

name: investment-banking-analysis
title: Investment-Banking Analysis
description: Perform transaction, valuation, capital-structure, and public-company analysis with auditable assumptions.
procedure:
1. Separate sourced inputs, task assumptions, and calculated values.
2. Normalize units, signs, periods, and share counts before computing.
3. Build the requested bridge or valuation in a traceable order.
4. Cross-check key outputs with an independent identity or reasonableness test.
notes: Do not silently mix fiscal periods, currencies, or enterprise and equity values.

name: management-consulting-synthesis
title: Management-Consulting Synthesis
description: Structure ambiguous business evidence into a clear analysis, implication, and recommendation.
procedure:
1. Restate the decision and define a mutually exclusive analysis structure.
2. Extract only evidence relevant to each branch and quantify it where possible.
3. Convert observations into implications, trade-offs, and prioritized actions.
4. Present the answer at the requested executive depth with assumptions visible.
notes: A recommendation should follow from the evidence rather than precede it.

name: quantitative-calculation-and-rounding
title: Quantitative Calculation and Rounding
description: Compute requested business or legal quantities with explicit formulas, units, precision, and rounding.
procedure:
1. Transcribe every input with its source, unit, sign, and period.
2. Write the formula before substituting values.
3. Retain full precision through intermediate calculations.
4. Apply the requested rounding only to the final displayed result and validate units.
notes: Keep percentages and decimal rates distinct throughout the calculation.

name: source-grounded-analysis
title: Source-Grounded Analysis
description: Read the supplied records and base every material conclusion on recoverable source evidence.
procedure:
1. Inventory the relevant supplied sources before drawing conclusions.
2. Extract the exact facts, dates, definitions, and units needed by the prompt.
3. Separate direct evidence from calculations and inference.
4. Recheck each final claim against a named source or a transparent derivation.
notes: Do not substitute general knowledge when the environment contains task-specific evidence.

name: scenario-comparison-and-sensitivity
title: Scenario Comparison and Sensitivity
description: Compare cases consistently and explain which assumptions drive the result.
procedure:
1. Hold common assumptions constant and isolate the variable that changes by case.
2. Apply the same formula, period, and units to every case.
3. Present absolute and relative differences where useful.
4. Identify the assumptions with the greatest decision impact and test edge cases.
notes: A valid comparison uses a common baseline and definition set.

name: financial-modeling-and-valuation
title: Financial Modeling and Valuation
description: Construct or review DCF, LBO, merger, trading-comps, and accretion/dilution analyses.
patterns: \b(?:dcf|discounted cash flow|lbo|leveraged buyout|merger model|accretion|dilution|trading comps|precedent transactions|valuation model)\b
procedure:
1. Map the requested model structure and source each operating and transaction assumption.
2. Build schedules in dependency order from operating case through valuation or returns.
3. Preserve formula consistency across periods and scenarios.
4. Reconcile cash flows, balance checks, valuation bridges, and stated outputs.
notes: Avoid hard-coding calculated outputs where a formula relationship is required.

name: spreadsheet-model-construction
title: Spreadsheet Model Construction
description: Create or update an auditable spreadsheet with formulas, formatting, labels, and checks.
procedure:
1. Inspect the workbook structure and preserve required tabs, labels, and existing formulas.
2. Separate inputs, calculations, outputs, and checks.
3. Use formulas for derived values and consistent professional formatting.
4. Reopen the workbook and verify formulas, links, totals, and requested output locations.
notes: Preserve templates and never replace formulas with unexplained hard-coded values.

name: professional-document-drafting
title: Professional Document Drafting
description: Create a structured professional memo, report, letter, or agreement in Word.
procedure:
1. Determine the audience, purpose, required sections, and source set.
2. Draft a clear hierarchy with a conclusion-led opening and evidence-backed body.
3. Apply consistent headings, tables, citations, and professional formatting.
4. Review the saved document for completeness, internal consistency, and visual legibility.
notes: The artifact must satisfy both substantive and presentation requirements.

name: presentation-storylining
title: Presentation Storylining
description: Create or revise an executive slide deck with a coherent storyline and evidence-led exhibits.
procedure:
1. Translate the decision into a sequence of takeaway headlines.
2. Assign one primary message and supporting exhibit to each slide.
3. Keep layouts, labels, sources, and visual encodings consistent.
4. Read the deck end to end and verify that every requested conclusion is evidenced.
notes: Slide titles should state the takeaway rather than merely name the topic.

name: business-correspondence
title: Business Email Correspondence
description: Search, interpret, draft, send, or reply to professional email while preserving context and recipients.
procedure:
1. Locate and read the complete relevant thread and attachments.
2. Preserve the subject, recipients, factual context, and requested tone.
3. Draft a concise response that answers every request and distinguishes decisions from open items.
4. Verify recipients and attachments before sending or replying.
notes: A request to answer in the task console is not itself permission to send email.

name: team-chat-communication
title: Team-Chat Communication
description: Read channel context and post concise, correctly threaded team-chat updates.
procedure:
1. Read the relevant channel history and thread before responding.
2. Extract the decision, action, owner, and deadline the update must convey.
3. Post in the requested channel or thread without duplicating messages.
4. Confirm the message is visible in the intended context.
notes: Use a thread reply when the task points to an existing discussion.

name: calendar-coordination
title: Calendar Coordination
description: Inspect availability and create or update meetings with correct attendees, time, and context.
procedure:
1. Resolve timezone, duration, attendees, and scheduling constraints.
2. Inspect existing events before selecting or changing a time.
3. Create or update exactly one event with an informative title and description.
4. Re-read the event and confirm time, attendees, and duplicate avoidance.
notes: Never assume a timezone when the source context specifies one.

name: sec-filing-research
title: SEC Filing Research
description: Find the correct issuer filing, period, form, and cited disclosure before extracting facts.
procedure:
1. Confirm issuer, form type, filing date, and reporting period.
2. Retrieve the authoritative filing and locate the relevant section or table.
3. Record units, period, and any restatement or non-GAAP qualification.
4. Cite the filing and reconcile extracted values to the requested calculation.
notes: Do not mix filing date, report date, or trailing-period metrics.

name: market-data-research
title: Market Data Research
description: Retrieve security identity, price, market capitalization, and public-company financial data consistently.
patterns: \b(?:ticker|share price|stock price|market capitalization|market cap|trading price|financial statements?)\b
procedure:
1. Resolve the correct company, ticker, exchange, and requested as-of date.
2. Retrieve the metric from the appropriate endpoint and retain its units and timestamp.
3. Normalize currency, shares, and fiscal period before combining sources.
4. Record the source and validate the result against a second reported identity when available.
notes: Latest price and historical as-of price are not interchangeable.

name: legal-drafting-and-redlining
title: Legal Drafting and Redlining
description: Draft or revise legal language while preserving defined terms, internal references, and requested risk allocation.
procedure:
1. Identify the requested legal effect and the provisions it depends on.
2. Preserve defined terms, numbering, cross-references, and document hierarchy.
3. Make the smallest language change that achieves the requested allocation or conclusion.
4. Check consistency across related provisions and summarize material changes.
notes: Do not alter unrelated provisions or silently introduce undefined terms.

name: executive-summary-and-recommendation
title: Executive Summary and Recommendation
description: Deliver a concise conclusion, supporting evidence, implications, and next actions for a professional audience.
procedure:
1. Lead with the answer to the decision question.
2. Support it with the few most material quantified or sourced findings.
3. State implications, risks, and uncertainty explicitly.
4. End with prioritized actions or next steps when requested.
notes: Concise means selective, not unsupported.

name: evidence-citation-and-traceability
title: Evidence Citation and Traceability
description: Attach recoverable sources, sections, pages, dates, and calculation lineage to important claims.
procedure:
1. Capture source identity and location while researching rather than after drafting.
2. Link each material factual claim to a document, page or section, date, or record.
3. Show calculation lineage from sourced inputs to result.
4. Verify that every citation resolves to the claimed evidence.
notes: A generic source list is weaker than claim-level traceability.

name: artifact-editing-and-template-preservation
title: Artifact Editing and Template Preservation
description: Update an existing office artifact without destroying its structure, formulas, styles, or unrelated content.
procedure:
1. Inspect the complete source artifact and identify protected structure.
2. Make changes in place or through a faithful copy as the task specifies.
3. Preserve unrelated content, formulas, styles, links, and metadata.
4. Reopen and compare the final artifact against the source and requested modifications.
notes: Recreating a template from scratch can silently drop formulas and formatting.

name: quality-control-and-cross-checking
title: Quality Control and Cross-Checking
description: Validate completeness, numerical consistency, artifact integrity, and requested formatting before finishing.
procedure:
1. Convert the prompt and rubric into a completion checklist.
2. Validate calculations with identities, bounds, and independent recomputation.
3. Reopen every produced artifact and inspect structure and visible content.
4. Confirm every requested output, format, recipient, and rounding rule before submission.
notes: Validation should test the saved deliverable, not only in-memory intermediates.
